description:
The consolidator persists no state: it rescans, replans and re-executes. This ticket is what earns that claim.

Assert the read-sequence invariant — identical {version, data} sequence for any target version — holds at EVERY intermediate state, not only before and after:

- interrupt between the pack write and the deletes
- interrupt part-way through the deletes
- run two consolidators against the same shard concurrently
- include a shard whose chunks straddle a cut boundary

The last case needs the known-committed version to lag by more than the cut interval, so that one cut flushes several buckets' worth of buffered data into a single chunk. No captured sample contains one (0 of 754 objects in /tmp/bedrock_00000), so it must be built synthetically rather than assumed rare enough to skip.

Expected outcomes: reads are correct and identical at every point; repeated runs converge rather than oscillate; concurrent runs produce identical bytes at identical keys, so both the puts and the deletes are idempotent.
title: Consolidator: interruption and concurrency tests
